declaration.context:
More general settings and state variables of the currently running game Ends the current round, regardless of timer state or player requests. Valid only if the server state is currently in any command phase
Describes wether the current game has ended. May be changed from false to true, but not the other way around. An ended game can only be resumed if a pre-ended savegame is loaded. If changed, all clients are notified of the ended game, and statistics are dispatched.
Retrieves the current round number Retrieves the current game phase. Due to their short duration, phases other than command phases or EndOfGame are rarely returned
Provides access to individual factions, both living and dead. Factions are primarily listed by unique ID. Use the 'names' or 'find' commands to retrieve the ID of a faction Lists the names along with the guid of all living factions. Dead factions are omitted
Finds and lists all living factions that contain the specified name parameter. Search is case-insensitive. Dead factions are omitted.

Settings related to the current world
Enables or liquid expansion. Lava and water will expand horizontally and downwards, and eventually floodfill all available space. No actual simulation at this stage. Liquid volume increases as long as connected space is available. Set false to disable.
Information visible to factions out front. 'None' will send two types of terrain information: 'Clear' and 'Unknown' where 'Unknown' accounts for all non-clear terrain types, including water and lava. 'Oceans' will separately expose all water. 'Liquids' will expose all liquids in general (currently water and lava). 'FullTerrain' exposes all initial terrain information to all clients (excluding terrain modifications caused by subsequent changes, e.g. nexus base construction).
Sets a custom Lua resource destribution script. Set to '' to use the internal distribution script. Any non-empty string X implies that [installDir]\lua\distributions\X.lua exists and is a valid Lua script. If the required script does not exist or cannot be executed, then the internal program is used instead, which uses the planet-specific density and max values.
The following defines which planet type to use. For any given string *X, a valid file [my documents]/My Games/Hexaverse/server/config/myPlanets/[X].ini must exist. For any given string X (without preceeding *), a valid file [install]/predefinedPlanets/[X].ini must exist.
Floating point 0 (none visible) to 1 (very dense)
Describes the content of the inner-most sphere of the planet. Use 'Clear' to make the inner core hollow. Depending on this setting, certain (or all) vehicles will be unable to stand on the bottom layer. Lava is always nice.
Describes the first layer of matter around the core. This layer will replace any matter formed by [Mountains]
Terrain content to fill the extended core with. The extended core reaches from the bottom most layer up to a height level corresponding to the remaining configuration of [ExtendedCore]. The core itself it not altered by these settings. Common scenarios include Lava or something hard like Granite. Less common, but sometimes nice is to set this to 'Clear', which will carve caves atop the inner core.
Central height of extended core matter. The terrain content specified in [type] will replace matter up to height=baseHeight+[random value]*noiseHeightScale, so chosing a low value might be a good idea.
Vertical noise stretching. Non-negative floating point. 0.0 will create a perfectly flat sphere at height baseHeight. 1 will be fairly mountainous, more is usually overkill.
Frequency of noise evolution. The higher, the thinner, sharper and more frequent mountains occur. Doesn't affect their height but will create a lot of pointy needles if too high. Lower values can be used to relax the terrain
Height levels above and below zero that are collapsed to zero to create an overall flatter terrain. E.g. if this is set to 2 then any resulting random height-level ([random value]*noiseHeightScale) that is -2,-1,0,1, or 2 will be interpreted as 0. Using any non-zero setting will result in flat valleys near the median height (baseHeight).
Type to fill mountains with. 'Unknown' attempts to guess what is best and may also selectively replace top under certain circumstances. Using 'Unknown' will chose mostly 'Rock'. 'Earth' is chosen only if appropriate by height, and top is set to 'Earth', 'Grass', 'Sand', or 'Snow'
Height level at which snow will occur. Set to 16+ to disable snow. Snow will replace the top most block in this layer, and selectively override top.
Same as ExtendedCore.baseHeight except for the mountain layer. Should be set to something much bigger than ExtendedCore.baseHeight>, since any matter generated by this layer will be replaced by [ExtendedCore].
Vertical noise stretching. Non-negative floating point. 0.0 will create a perfectly flat sphere at height baseHeight. 1 will be fairly mountainous, more is usually overkill.
Frequency of noise evolution. The higher, the thinner, sharper and more frequent mountains occur. Doesn't affect their height but will create a lot of pointy needles if too high. Lower values can be used to relax the terrain.
Height levels above and below zero that are collapsed to zero to create an overall flatter terrain. E.g. if this is set to 2 then any resulting random height-level ([random value]*noiseHeightScale) that is -2,-1,0,1, or 2 will be interpreted as 0. Using any non-zero setting will result in flat valleys near the median height (baseHeight).

Game rule settings
None: No AI bases, no winning rules other than killing everyone else. ConquerNexus: Three AI bases are spawned around the globe. Their center Nexus Ports must be conquered by building anything next to it. Additional Nexus Ports are spawned if EMP zones are active. Two/three (depending on number of unlocked zones) Nexus Ports must be conquered to win.
Comma-separated list of supported faction types. Indicates that new factions can be created only during round 0.
Time in seconds that players can remain in command phase. once the deadline is reached, rounds will be progressed. Set negative or zero to deactivate.
If set true, then any unit carrying a Bomb-turret will trigger self-detonation on uncontrolled death. Self-detonation is not triggered by Demolish commands. New players are given minimal bases (that meet the constraints of basesRequired) Indicates that players must maintain minimal bases to be considered 'alive'. Minimal bases include a mandatory compound capable of generating infinite amounts of minerals. Such a compound includes a live mine that can deliver at least 10 units of fuel, one that can deliver at least 5 units of minerals, and a generator. Additionally, the player must own at least one terraformer or a vehicle plant that can be switched on. If any one of these conditions is not met, a death counter will count down each round for the respective faction, until it reaches zero. If it does, all vehicles and structures of that faction are destroyed. If the game is closed and only one faction remains, that faction is declared victor. Sends effective vehicle initiative to hostile factions
New offensive vehicles using normal ammunition start with full ammo. Effective only for vehicles actually requiring ammunition, and using default ammunition.
Maximum possible uplink bandwidth per faction. Effective only when uplink bandwidth system is enabled. Currently not.
Configures treatment of doomsday-weaponry. 'Expose' will notify clients of both the explosion and resulting crater even if they cannot actually see the explosion. 'Conceal' will treat them like ordinary weaponry: if explosion and/or affected terrain are in scanning range, the effects will be partially or completely visible.
The maximum number of allowed factions per unlocked zone. If more factions are created, more zones will be unlocked. The resulting number of unlocked zones is rounded up. Example: factionsPerEMPZone set to 3 causes the first three factions to share the same zone. The fourth faction will permanently unlock a new zone. This value cannot be increased if any factions (besides the Nexus faction) exist.
Establishes auto-retracting EMP zones that constraint player expansion depending on faction-count. Initially the EMP zones will cover most of the planet. As faction count increases, EMP zones will slowly retract to expose more terrain to expand into. If enabled and gameGoal is set to ConquerNexus, then secondary Nexus Ports will be spawned on poles that are not covered by Nexus stations. Enabling this value on a live session (via the control console) will fail if any factions exist (the Nexus faction does not count). Otherwise EMP zones may be enabled or disabled as desired, but the presence of Nexus Ports remains unaffected prior to constructing a new world.
Total number of structures/vehicles that may be deployed by any one faction. Only deployment is counted. Vehicles may be stored in vehicle stores to avoid being counted. Specifies whether or not unit limits should be applied. Limits for buildings
Limits for mobile turrets. The used base, if variable, is ignored.
Nexus faction settings If enabled, then Nexus bases are constructed around 3 of the 12 planet poles. Only affects newly created worlds. True if the local world has spawned Nexus bases. If enabled, then Nexus Ports are spawned at all 12 pole locations. This setting is forcefully applied if gameGoal is set to ConquerNexus and empZones are on. True if the local world has spawned Nexus Ports on all 12 poles.
Enables the AI to process units of the Nexus faction. Spawns nexus vehicles, and AI client to control nexus vehicles/structures (if any). A client is separately launched to compute AI decisions.
Linearly affects density of nexus vehicles. If density is saturated, vehicle production/spawning halts.
The number of rounds necessary for the Nexus faction to gain one research point in every endless research topic. Set 0 to disable Nexus research.
List of turrets that the AI will spawn if 'nexus' is set to true. Only affects newly created vehicles - does not affect nexus vehicles loaded from a save-file.
